title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.
intro: This training programme equips FIU analysts and managers to turn suspicious transaction reports and other information into timely, well-targeted financial intelligence through sound operational and strategic analysis, dissemination and international cooperation.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give FIU analysts and their managers a practical grounding in the full intelligence cycle, from receiving and prioritising reports through operational and strategic analysis to dissemination and feedback. Participants leave able to produce intelligence that investigators can act on, identify trends and typologies for policy-makers and reporting entities, and use domestic and international cooperation channels with confidence.
sections.What It Covers: The FIU's mandate and models, the FATF standards for financial intelligence, receipt and triage of suspicious transaction reports, information sources and access, operational analysis techniques, strategic analysis and typologies, dissemination and use of intelligence, feedback and outreach to reporting entities, international cooperation through the Egmont Group, and data, analytics and measuring effectiveness.
Intended Audience: Operational and strategic analysts in financial intelligence units
FIU heads of analysis, team leaders and staff managing intake, dissemination and international cooperation
Investigators and liaison officers who request, receive or rely on FIU intelligence
Learning Objectives: Explain the FIU's core functions, models and obligations under the FATF standards
Design risk-based processes to receive, triage and prioritise suspicious transaction reports
Apply operational analysis techniques to identify targets, networks and money flows
Produce strategic analysis that identifies trends, typologies and vulnerabilities
Disseminate intelligence effectively and give useful feedback to reporting entities
Use Egmont Group channels, data tools and performance measures to strengthen the FIU's impact
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with case exercises and analytical worked examples, ending in an analysis workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the FIU's model and priorities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial intelligence, investigation or AML/CFT work is helpful. No specialist analytical or data science background is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
Egmont Group (2013), Principles for Information Exchange Between Financial Intelligence Units
Egmont Group (2013, as updated), Operational Guidance for FIU Activities and the Exchange of Information
FATF (2013, as updated), Methodology for Assessing Technical Compliance with the FATF Recommendations and the Effectiveness of AML/CFT Systems

modules.title: The FIU: Mandate, Models and International Standards
modules.summary: The FIU's place in the national AML/CFT system: its core functions, the administrative, law-enforcement, judicial and hybrid models, and what the FATF standards and effectiveness assessments expect.
objectives: Explain the receipt, analysis and dissemination functions of an FIU
Compare FIU models and their implications for powers and access to information
Summarise what FATF Recommendation 29 and Immediate Outcome 6 require
syllabus: Core functions: receipt, analysis and dissemination
Administrative, law-enforcement, judicial and hybrid models
Operational independence, autonomy and protection of information
FATF Recommendation 29, Immediate Outcome 6 and common evaluation findings

modules.title: Receiving and Prioritising Suspicious Transaction Reports
modules.summary: How reports and other disclosures arrive, how their quality is checked, and how a risk-based triage process directs scarce analytical resource to the cases that matter most.
objectives: Describe the main report types and disclosures received by the FIU
Assess report quality and recognise common reporting weaknesses
Design a risk-based triage and prioritisation model
syllabus: Suspicious transaction reports, threshold reports and cross-border declarations
Reporting quality: defensive reporting, gaps and data standards
Triage criteria, risk scoring and case selection
Managing backlogs, urgent requests and time-critical cases

modules.title: Information Sources and Access
modules.summary: The information an FIU can draw on, from its own holdings to law-enforcement, administrative and open sources, and the legal and practical limits on obtaining and using it.
objectives: Identify the domestic information sources available to analysts
Request further information from reporting entities effectively
Use open-source and commercial data lawfully and with appropriate verification
syllabus: FIU holdings and law-enforcement, tax, customs and registry data
Requests for further information from reporting entities
Open-source intelligence: value, verification and safeguards
Data protection, confidentiality and handling restrictions

modules.title: Operational Analysis: Techniques and Tradecraft
modules.summary: Core methods for turning reports and data into actionable intelligence on specific targets, including link and network analysis, flow-of-funds analysis and the development and testing of hypotheses.
objectives: Apply link, network and flow-of-funds analysis to case data
Develop and test hypotheses about suspected criminal activity
Evaluate source reliability and grade intelligence consistently
syllabus: The analytical process: collation, evaluation, analysis and inference
Link charts, network analysis and timelines
Flow-of-funds and transaction pattern analysis
Hypothesis testing, cognitive bias and source grading

modules.title: Operational Analysis in Practice: Common Case Types
modules.summary: How operational analysis is applied to the cases FIUs see most often, from fraud and corruption to drug trafficking, tax crime and terrorist financing, and the financial indicators each tends to show.
objectives: Recognise the financial footprint of the main predicate offences
Apply case-specific indicators to prioritise and develop analysis
Identify when a case needs specialist or multi-agency input
syllabus: Fraud, corruption and politically exposed persons
Drug trafficking, organised crime and cash-intensive laundering
Tax crime, trade-based laundering and professional enablers
Terrorist financing and sanctions-related reports

modules.title: Strategic Analysis, Typologies and Risk Assessment
modules.summary: How FIUs use aggregated data to identify trends, typologies and vulnerabilities, and how strategic products inform national risk assessments, policy-making and supervisory priorities.
objectives: Distinguish strategic from operational analysis and their audiences
Design a strategic analysis project from question to finished product
Contribute FIU findings to national and sectoral risk assessments
syllabus: Purposes and audiences of strategic analysis
Methods: trend analysis, aggregated data and environmental scanning
Writing typologies and red-flag indicators
Informing national risk assessment, policy and supervisory priorities

modules.title: Dissemination and Use of Financial Intelligence
modules.summary: How intelligence is packaged and disseminated spontaneously and on request, how its use is tracked, and how FIUs balance timeliness, source protection and the needs of recipients.
objectives: Prepare intelligence products that recipients can act on
Apply dissemination rules, handling conditions and source protection
Track the use and outcomes of disseminated intelligence
syllabus: Spontaneous and on-request dissemination
Writing for investigators, prosecutors, tax and supervisory recipients
Handling codes, onward use and protecting reporters
Tracking use, outcomes and case feedback

modules.title: Feedback, Outreach and Reporting Entities
modules.summary: How FIUs improve reporting quality through case-specific and general feedback, guidance and outreach, and work with supervisors to address persistent weaknesses in reporting sectors.
objectives: Design effective general and case-specific feedback to reporting entities
Identify under-reporting and poor-quality reporting by sector
Coordinate with supervisors on reporting compliance
syllabus: Forms of feedback: case-specific, sectoral and typology-based
Guidance, red-flag indicators and outreach programmes
Measuring report quality and sector reporting patterns
Working with supervisors on reporting failures

modules.title: International Cooperation and the Egmont Group
modules.summary: How FIUs exchange information with foreign counterparts through Egmont Group channels and bilateral arrangements, the principles governing exchange, and how to make and answer requests well.
objectives: Explain the Egmont Group principles for information exchange
Prepare clear, well-founded requests and timely responses
Manage consent, onward dissemination and cooperation with non-counterparts
syllabus: The Egmont Group, its secure channel and membership expectations
Principles of exchange: reciprocity, prior consent and confidentiality
Drafting requests and spontaneous disclosures
Diagonal cooperation and cross-border case coordination

modules.title: Data, Analytics and FIU Effectiveness: Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining data and analytics tools and performance measurement, ending with a case workshop that runs the full intelligence cycle.
objectives: Assess how data platforms and analytics can strengthen FIU work
Define meaningful measures of FIU performance and impact
Apply the full intelligence cycle to a realistic case
syllabus: Data platforms, data matching, network analytics and machine learning
Responsible and explainable use of advanced analytics
Performance measures: outputs, outcomes and effectiveness
Workshop: from report intake to dissemination

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.

related.title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle tax crime and related laundering through information exchange and joint investigation.
